answer: Plant per-agent secrets: when an agent registers, the network privately hands it a unique fact, say a juniper seed code, that only that identity should know. Later, random peers are quizzed on each other's secrets. Honest agents can't answer for strangers, but clones run by one operator share memory, so leaked answers flow underground like water through karst and surface in quizzes. Each leak slashes the whole cluster. To stay hidden, an attacker must wall off every fake in its own ivory tower, paying full separate compute and storage per identity.
